title: A shared component arrives the size it should be in this document
goal: A component built on a Retina screenshot is drawn in image pixels, so dropping it into a document that is one to one makes it arrive twice as big as it looks where it was made. It should arrive the size a person expects, whatever document it came from.
notes: Sources/PhotonzCore/SharedComponents.swift: adoptSharedComponent takes the drawing verbatim. The starters solve this by BUILDING at max(pixelScale, 1); a shared component is a drawing rather than a recipe, so it needs scaling on the way in (LayerScaling) plus a note of the scale it was shared at on SharedComponent. Raised by the audit queue/audits/2026-09-12-shared-components.json.
acceptance: A component shared from a document at pixel scale 2 and dropped into one at pixel scale 1 arrives at the same apparent size it had where it was made
A component shared and dropped between two documents at the same scale is unchanged from today

log.note: Reproduced on HEAD first: a component made in a pixelScale-2 document arrived at 120x40 with 24pt type in a pixelScale-1 document, where 60x20 / 12pt was wanted. Temp test printed 'ARRIVED SIZE: (120.0, 40.0) font: 24.0'.

Adversarial review before building: the mock/audit says 'starters solve this by rebuilding at the document scale; a shared component cannot'. Correct, but the note stopped at the drop. The drop is only half of it: refill() rewrites the local drawing from the shelf after every sync, so a component that arrived right would have been put back to the shelf's numbers on the next look. Both ways in rescale now.

Design: magnified(by:) was the obvious tool and is the wrong one. It deliberately leaves content payloads (type size, stroke width, outline points) alone because the rasterizer is handed a box plus a scale. A shared component STAYS in the new document, so the type has to move with the box or a halved button keeps 24pt words. Hence a separate Layer.rescaled(by:) in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerRescaling.swift.
Shelf format: SharedComponent.pixelScale is optional. A shelf written before this decodes nil and its drawings are taken verbatim, so nothing already on anybody's shelf moves.
No ping-pong risk between two open windows: sharedShelfChanged goes through applyOutsideHistory, which does not publish, so a sync never republishes. Only a person's edit publishes.

Added an optional pixelScale to the walk harness's blank step (PlaytestScript + PlaytestHarness + docs/design/playtest-harness.md), because there was no way for a walk to make two documents that count differently. It drives the same setDocumentPixelScale the capture-scale control uses.

left rough: a component that MOVES is not rescaled - LayerMotion values keep the numbers they were written with. Nothing on the shelf animates yet and motion-on-components is not a shipped combination, so it did not earn a task; it is in the audit's rough list.
left rough: a measure's labelScale is left alone on purpose (a readout is a fixed size by design), so a caliper inside a shared component would keep its readout size across a crossing.
Screen was LOCKED for this whole task, so no walk could run: shared-component-scale-walk.json parses but has never been executed, and the audit has no pictures at all. Sweep requested.

The shelf now records the unit a drawing was written in and both ways into a document restate it: Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerRescaling.swift (new Layer.rescaled(by:)) plus SharedComponents.swift. Verified by reproducing the bug on HEAD first (120x40/24pt where 60x20/12pt was wanted), then 13 new tests covering both directions, same-scale, an old shelf with no scale recorded, and the round trip through sync; full suite 7466 tests green.
